newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai court jails three Australians for drugs.
newsitem.headline: Thai court jails three Australians for drugs.

text.p: Thailand's Criminal Court on Monday sentenced three Australians -- a man and two women -- to 50 years in jail each on charges of trafficking in heroin, a court official said.
The official said the judge initially sentenced Lyle Doniger, 44, Jane McKenzie, 30, and Deborah Spinner, 29, to life imprisonment but later commuted the term of 50 years in jail for each of them.
All of them could appeal their sentence in the Appeals Court before April 30, the official told Reuters.

The three Australians, all from Sydney, were arrested at Bangkok airport on March 22, 1996 as they were about to board a flight home after customs agents found a total of 350 grams (12.5 ounces) of heroin in their possession.
After the sentence, the three were taken by police to jail pending any appeal.

Under Thai criminal law, possession of more than 20 grams (0.7 ounces) of heroin is regarded as an attempt to traffic in drugs. Heroin trafficking carries the maximum of a death penalty in Thailand but the sentence is invariably commuted to a lengthy prison term.
